references.text: Jesus says that whoever receives one of his disciples receives him. The same principle about receiving in Jesus' name.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus places a little child among the disciples and speaks about receiving such a child in his name, as well as humbling oneself like the child.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus takes a little child, sets it among them, and says that whoever receives such a child in his name receives him.
Jesus identifies with the least: "Whatever you did for one of these my least brothers, you did for me." The same principle that serving the small is serving Christ.
Jesus says that whoever receives the one he sends receives him, and whoever receives him receives the one who sent him. The same chain of representation.
Jesus says that whoever believes in him believes not only in him but in the one who sent him. The same thought that receiving Jesus is receiving the Father.
Jesus says that whoever hears the disciples hears him, and whoever rejects them rejects him and the one who sent him. The same chain of representation.
Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted. Related to the statement that the least among you is great.
Jesus says that the greatest among them should be like the youngest, and the leader like a servant. A direct parallel to the idea that the least is great.
The greatest among you shall be your servant. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted. The same teaching about greatness through humility.
Jesus says that whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all. A parallel to the statement that the least among you is great.
Peter urges the young to submit to the elders, for God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. Humility as the path to greatness in God's kingdom.
